proof_origin.place: K-flat localization comparisons; S4 reuses the independent-universe lifting isomorphism and the homotopy acyclicity characterization

lean.statement:
theorem schemeTensorShift_targetComparison_isIso
    (P T U : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := X.sheaf) P)
    (hT : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := X.sheaf) T)
    (hU : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := X.sheaf) U) :
    letI := schemeCanonicalTensorShift X
    letI : ∀ B : schemeDerivedCategory X, (tensorRight B).CommShift ℤ :=
      fun B ↦ Functor.CommShift₂.commShiftFlipObj (h := .int) B
    IsIso (schemeTensorShiftTargetComparison X P T U)

proof.text: Convert the sheaf IsKFlat hypotheses for P and T to the monoidal quasi-isomorphism kFlat predicate. The homotopy-category characterization asks that tensoring preserve acyclic objects on both sides; the given hypothesis proves the right-tensor case and the braiding gives the left-tensor case.

For a kFlat complex V, the component of IndependentTensorShift.TensorCommShift₂.liftingIsoHom at V and any W is the Qh tensorator and is invertible. Transport through quotientCompQhIso; the tensorator of the quotient functor is invertible, so the composite tensorator of Q is invertible as well.

Apply this to (T,U) and (P,T tensor U). The target comparison is the shift of the composite of the whiskered first tensorator and the second tensorator, followed by the inverse localization shift comparison. All these maps are isomorphisms, hence so is their composite. No K-flatness of U is needed for this component.
